System-level Simulations The defined use case scenarios in Task 2 were analyzed for 2 different conditions. One with fixed LTC, regulator taps, and cap controls disabled and the other with active LTC, regulator taps, and cap controls as presented in Table 4. The updated EV charging sites were considered, and the existing PVs were removed to focus on the SST impact on the grid. In the later phase, PV+storage are installed at the sites and the operation of SST with PV+storage was studied. 16 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications. Table 4. Voltage: The overall minimum and maximum voltages on the feeder through the simulation day are shown in Fig. 17, In scenario 1 with EV only, the minimum voltage goes beyond the ANSI limit of 0.95 per unit in the presence of high EV charging load. It’s clear that the low voltage beyond 0.95 occurred whenever there is high coincidental EV charging. On the other hand, in scenario 2, when SST was added instead of conventional transformers, the minimum voltages were greatly improved. Even though the minimum voltages were raised significantly, the overall feeder minimum voltages were below 0.95 for high EV charging hours. This implies that the J1 feeder LTC, regulators and capacitors are required to be active for the feeder’s daily operation. 17 This report is available at no cost from NREL at www.nrel.gov/publications.
